parsed.explanation: Article 521 directly criminalises trans feminine presentation with up to six years, reaching any outed visitor, and the country review finds de facto and explicit criminalisation targeting trans women. Enforcement apparatus is documented: police arrests of LGBT people, prosecutor-ordered anal examinations, a 36-person raid, an interior ministry ban on gatherings, and an activist arrest. Regional asylum guidance treats LGBTIQ claims from this country as a distinct risk category — strong evidence the state itself is understood as a source of danger. Legal gender recognition is unavailable and trans people face policing and documentation barriers; documented rises in prejudice and violence add societal exposure. Courts have pushed back on Article 534 and froze the 2022 assembly order, but Article 521 stands unchallenged, so institutional counterweight does not protect against the operative trans-specific offence. No visitor-specific screening or custody data is documented, but explicit criminalisation plus recorded enforcement places this below the 0.25 tier.
